final.investment_thesis:
The rating is Hold because the debate is balanced after weighing, not because the seats disagreed — the aggressive, conservative and neutral analysts all arrived at the same 2.0% total target from different mandates (alpha capture, capital preservation, risk budgeting), and none of their stated disagreements change the executable number. I adopt that convergence rather than manufacturing a direction.

What the bulls win, and it is not trivial. The supplied fundamentals are strong and unrebutted: 9M FY26 revenue +16.1%, net income +20.0%, diluted EPS +22.4%, Q3 gross margin 50.06% with +357 bps YoY expansion, gross profit growth accelerating three quarters, normalized 9M FCF +37.5%, $146.5B cash and securities, $62.2B net cash, and no new long-term debt. Price at 313.45 sits 11.1% above a rising 200-SMA at 282.12 with the 50/200 spread widening to 29.10, and Bollinger bandwidth has compressed to 8.46%, the narrowest in 60 sessions — a directional resolution is close, so zero exposure is an active bet against the dominant structure. The aggressive analyst was right that the conservative's use of ~32x forward earnings to deny all upside is overreach: the margin expansion is the company's own reported data, not an extrapolation.

What the bears win, and it is equally concrete. 313.45 clears the 50-SMA by 0.72% and the VWMA (309.11) by 1.4%; the MACD histogram has flipped positive (+0.152) while the line remains below zero at -1.10; the 8/20 rejection at 320.28 stands with an unfilled 7/31 gap overhead; and the +1.15% up-day came on 34.0M shares, 68% of the 20-day average. That is repair, not breakout. The bear is also correct that VWMA, Bollinger mid and the 50-SMA are correlated price averages, not three independent signals, and that a ~2% stop on a name with 2.29% ATR is noise-width rather than risk control. Those arguments cap the position; they do not justify exit against this balance sheet.

Sizing, weighed against both tails. At the retained 2.01%, an 8.5% AAPL rally to the 340.08 area contributes only ~0.17% to total account return, while a 10% decline costs ~0.20%; a stop-line break toward 306.00 is roughly -$48, or ~0.05% of equity. The cash-opportunity-cost of the 97.99% non-interest-bearing cash balance is real and is the strongest argument for going higher, but it is not strong enough today: the upside path is gated by an unconfirmed 320.28 breakout, so adding now would be paying fees to front-run a trigger the plan itself says to wait for. A concrete higher allocation is 4-5%: it would require adding ~$2,000-$3,000 of cash at ~$2-$3 in 10-bps fees, and is justified only by a daily close above 320.28 on volume clearly above the 19-session ex-spike average (~45-55M), ideally 55M+, plus gross margin holding near 50%. A concrete lower allocation is 0%: it would free ~$2,010 for ~$2 in fees and eliminate downside, but it would surrender participation in the gap-fill path toward 327.74/333.43/340.08 and pay a certain cost to exit an unbroken primary trend. Neither boundary is justified by today's evidence.

Why 2% is a real position, not an observation placeholder. Its economic purpose is to hold a funded claim on the breakout path while the total risk to the account is capped near 0.05% of equity at the 306.00 line — a payoff profile that cannot be replicated by watching from zero, because re-entering after a confirmed 320.28 close means buying ~2.2% higher. That asymmetry, not the desire to 'keep an eye on it', is why 2% is preferable to 0% after fees. Equally, there is no case to raise merely to avoid a small percentage.

On the 8/24 trim: the prior move from ~5% to 2.0% was a deliberate total-target reassessment, not the start of a mechanical proportional-trimming sequence. I explicitly decline to trim again from 2% without fresh evidence beyond what was already weighed on 8/24 — the burden is on the seller now, and the levels that would shift it are stated below.

What would change the call. Upgrade toward Overweight/5%: a daily close above 320.28 on volume clearly above the 19-session ex-spike average with gross margin holding near 50%. Move toward Underweight/0%: two consecutive closes below 308.80, a close below 306.00, or a COGS-growth-over-revenue-growth trend for two quarters or gross margin below 48%. These are narrative conditions, not implemented orders; no stop or limit is placed from this plan, and the keep_shares decision now is separate from any future conditional add or cut. Stated gaps, not papered over: no segment/product/geographic revenue split, so 50.06% gross-margin durability cannot be attributed; no consensus estimate series or guidance, so the ~32x forward multiple is an unverified bridge; no options or implied-vol data, so no hedge can be priced; the news window 8/19-8/23 is missing with only ~20 of 92 records supplied, leaving the cause of the 7/31 gap unestablished and sentiment confidence discounted; and all targets here are technical, not valuation-derived.
